title: Tuberville and Britt introduce bill to tie USPS bonuses to performance metrics
text:
Tuberville and Britt introduce bill to tie USPS bonuses to performance metrics
N. C. Thorne
U.S. Senator Tommy Tuberville joined Senator Katie Britt in introducing the Postal Executive Responsibility, Fiscal Oversight, and Results-based Management (PERFORM) Act on Aug. 4. The proposed legislation aims to ensure that the Postmaster General’s performance pay is contingent upon meeting specific financial, operational, and reporting standards at the United States Postal Service.
According to Tuberville, “Millions of Americans rely on the U.S. Postal Service to receive bills, send invoices, and hear from their friends and family. In the private sector, if an organization is losing money every year, it would go under. The last thing we need to be doing is handing out bonuses to reward poor management. I’m glad to join Senator Britt to introduce this bill to provide accountability and incentivize better results out of the USPS.”
Britt said, “In just about any profession, you don’t get rewarded for failing—except at the United States Postal Service. It’s time that changed. This is not complicated: if the Postal Service does not meet basic performance metrics, the Postmaster General’s compensation should reflect that. No reasonable company in the world gives its CEO a bonus after failing to meet multiple performance metrics, and the Postmaster General—who serves the American people—should be no different.”
The PERFORM Act would prohibit awarding a performance-based bonus to the Postmaster General if during the previous fiscal year USPS reports a net loss; fails nationwide service targets; receives an adverse audit finding; or fails required Congressional reporting obligations. The legislation also mandates an annual report detailing executive bonuses and key USPS financial data within 30 days after each fiscal year ends and directs annual review by USPS Office of Inspector General.
The House version of this legislation has been introduced by Representative Dale Strong with cosponsorship from Alabama's full congressional delegation.
Tuberville represents Alabama in several Senate committees including Armed Services; Agriculture; Veterans’ Affairs; HELP; and Aging, according to the official website. He previously built a four-decade career as a college football coach at institutions such as Auburn University.
